    },
    {
      "login": "l0rinc",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "requested changes on locator/in-memory desync causing corruption on interrupt, loop bounds, eager flat file writing, and lack of explanation for refactors"
    },
    {
      "login": "hebasto",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "noted IWYU include issue resolved in #34498"
    },
    {
      "login": "maflcko",
      "stance": "question",
      "note": "asked about running tests across all commits and noted unrelated CI test failures"
    },
    {
      "login": "Jhackman2019",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "reported clean build and test pass on ARM64"
    },
    {
      "login": "bvbfan",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "pointed out a non-existent function call in txindex.cpp"
    },
    {
      "login": "optout21",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "crACK after discussions on batching logic and lock contention reduction"
    },
    {
      "login": "arejula27",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Concept ACK; reported interrupt handling bug and removing final (both resolved); helping rebase and benchmarking"
    },
    {
      "login": "sedited",
      "stance": "question",
      "note": "asked about BlockBatch usage, NextSyncBlock design, and potential memory pressure"
    },
    {
      "login": "sipa",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "clarified that the iterator reordering refactor does not alter execution behavior"
    },
    {
      "login": "polespinasa",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK during PR review club; suggested clearer commit messages on refactors"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "rc:2807338683",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Early return in ProcessBlocks bypassed interrupt handling, skipping the expected recovery and commit path",
      "quote": "Returning `false` here causes the interrupt to be handled incorrectly... As a result, the expected recovery path is skipped.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author replied in rc:2807692937; fixed by rc:2807692937",
      "author_replies": ["rc:2807692937"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2807692937",
      "status_by_quote": "Nice catch. Pushed an update that fixes it and adds test coverage."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2884888266",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Removing final from BlockFilterIndex weakens class encapsulation solely to allow test subclassing",
      "quote": "Im not sure if removing `final` from `BlockFilterIndex` only to allow `IndexBlockSim` to subclass it for **testing** is the better decision",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author replied in rc:2885860031; fixed by c:4000080225",
      "author_replies": ["rc:2885860031"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:4000080225",
      "status_by_quote": "Updated per feedback. Thanks @arejula27."
    },
    {
      "id": "r:3744459738",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "In-memory index state advances ahead of persisted data during batching; an interrupt causes Commit() to write advanced state with a stale locator, corrupting the index on restart",
      "quote": "The most serious issue seems to me that `Commit()` during interrupt writes advanced `m_muhash` alongside a stale locator, which causes `CoinStatsIndex::CustomInit` to reject the index as corrupted on",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author acknowledged in c:5388740037 noting a missing check regarding the race condition that needs proper consideration",
      "author_replies": ["c:5388740037"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:5388740037",
      "status_by_quote": "there is just one missing check regarding the race condition that we should consider properly"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2905123979",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Commit claims to be a refactor with no behavior change but reorders iterator assignment before block processing without documenting the change or safety",
      "quote": "We're changing behavior in a commit that claims it's not a behavior change, without adding context for why this change was needed",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "contested",
      "status_note": "author replied in rc:2936981455 and sipa clarified in rc:2940970303, but l0rinc maintained in rc:2941160846 that commits should be squashed or documented",
      "author_replies": ["rc:2936981455", "rc:2940770445"],
      "other_replies": ["rc:2940970303"],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2941160846",
      "status_by_quote": "I think those commits should be squashed and the behavior change either fixed or documented."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2905545389",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "Unbounded backward loop in ProcessBlocks could loop infinitely or crash past genesis if start and end heights are invalid or on different forks",
      "quote": "Given how intertwined the code is here, a serious mess-up could cause an infinite loop and would be really hard to trace back to the source.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2906884044",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "BlockFilterIndex writes flat files to disk eagerly per block, which is misaligned with LevelDB batching and risks orphaned flat file data on interrupt",
      "quote": "We seem to be writing to disk to eagerly here, this also is misaligned with the batching.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "re-raised in rc:3882262247 asking if it can be fixed",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2758171790",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Why keep ProcessBlock around instead of handling one or many blocks in one function?",
      "quote": "Why keep `ProcessBlock` around? It should be simpler if we just have one function and it can be handed one or many blocks.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained specialization plans for parallelization in rc:2759661644",
      "author_replies": ["rc:2759661644"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2759661644",
      "status_by_quote": "Because `ProcessBlocks` will be specialized in a follow-up commit (please see #26966) to enable additional speedups"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2758183422",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Has the batch size been optimized with benchmarks or is that planned, possibly per-index?",
      "quote": "Has this been optimized with benchmarks or are you planning to do that? This might be something differs between the indexes so it might make sense to let each index define their own value.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "accepted",
      "status_note": "author replied in rc:2759584026 to handle in follow-up; fjahr accepted in rc:2935249122 noting benchmark results showed no penalty",
      "author_replies": ["rc:2759584026"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:2935249122",
      "status_by_quote": "the benchmarks have been run now and quite extensively and I haven't seen any penalty from this change. I think the follow-up that tweaks the value... if that is the case then I don't think my comment should be considered a blocker."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:2799911732",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Consider batching by transaction count rather than block count to make batch sizes and memory usage more uniform",
      "quote": "I suggest considering other approaches, such as a fixed transaction count (e.g., adding blocks until the number of transactions within them falls within a target range).",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained the trade-offs regarding parallelization in c:3892133978 and previous comments",
      "author_replies": ["c:3892133978"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:3892133978",
      "status_by_quote": "even if it runs at the same speed on an HDD (which I doubt), the other improvements this PR brings still make it worth it."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:4019533753",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "safety",
      "text": "What is the expected memory increase from batching and does it put undesirable memory pressure on the OS?",
      "quote": "What is the expectation on the increase of memory usage here? I tried profiling it with massif... Can we really batch operations in this way without putting more memory pressure on the OS?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author replied in c:4019669239 explaining why conservative batch size keeps memory overhead acceptable during initial sync",
      "author_replies": ["c:4019669239"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:4019669239",
      "status_by_quote": "The batch size is intentionally small. I was very conservative with the chosen value to avoid having to worry about it here."
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "c:3840520048",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "I prefer this over https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/33306 - and will investigate if this solves that problem once my benchmarking servers free up.",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "none",
      "areas": []
    },
    {
      "id": "c:3874191155",
      "verdict": "ACK",
      "reason": "LGTM after clarifications and changes! Code review, no assessment on performance.",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": ["src/index/base.cpp"]
    },
    {
      "id": "r:3792564543",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "I really like the idea and I think it will be a massive upgrade with your parallelisation proposal #26966",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "none",
      "areas": []
    },
    {
      "id": "r:4372795917",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "swift code review for the Spanish PR review club; noted commit messages could explain refactoring steps better",
      "substantive": false,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": ["src/index/base.cpp", "src/index/base.h"]
    }
  ],
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "author",
      "what": "rebase and addressing corruption race on interrupt and flat file writes",
      "id": "c:5388740037"
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Re-read and updated all claims and questions per schema rules. Added non-objection claims (questions from fjahr, sedited, and suggestion from arejula27) that were missing in schema 1. Marked r:3744459738 answered after furszy's acknowledgment in c:5388740037, and updated rc:2905123979 to contested following l0rinc's response to sipa and furszy."
}
